incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: autoscale-queue-depth-high fired in prod (priority: P1). Group: inference-serving. Trigger value: queue_depth=128 (threshold 100). Paging @sara @liam

sara: saw the page. I'm on it. grabbing logs and current autoscaler metrics.

liam: pinged — on laptop, will join in 2 minutes.

anna: noticed a spike in tokens/sec and concurrent requests around 16:07 UTC. Might be a burst from a batch job.

sara: initial customer impact: increased 429s and throttle events. Looking at telemetry: throttles up from ~5/min to ~60/min across clusters us-west-2. Enterprise customers affected: acct-redwood-inc and acct-finserv-1 reported elevated errors.

oliver: product side: acct-redwood-inc reported delays in chat generation, their latency went from 200ms -> 1.2s and some timeouts. They opened a support ticket.

sara: call out to oncall runbook: checking queue_depth, tokens/sec, throttle_events dashboards.

sara: running query: `sum by (cluster)(queue_depth) / sum by (cluster)(capacity_gpus)` and `rate(tokens_processed[1m])` to correlate.

liam: pasting quick results:```
cluster us-west-2: queue_depth=128, tokens/s=42000, throttle_events=58
cluster eu-central-1: queue_depth=12, tokens/s=8k, throttle_events=1
```

sara: so it's concentrated in us-west-2. Autoscaler didn't spin up fast enough because scale-up threshold is queue_depth > 150 for 3m. We hit 128 and stayed for 6m.

anna: looks like we have noisy alerting AND too-high scale trigger. Two things to handle: immediate mitigation + postmortem tuning.

sara: immediate actions: 1) trigger manual scale on us-west-2 (add 4 nodes), 2) enable temporary throttle fallback to model-variant-lt to reduce latency, 3) notify customers.

liam: executing manual scale now: `infractl scale --cluster us-west-2 --add 4`

incident-bot: Runbook step executed by liam: manual scale started at 2024-05-06T16:10:12Z.

sara: enabling fallback policy for 10m. Will route new requests to variant with smaller KV cache.

oliver: messaging to customers: pushing a short update to account contacts for the two affected customers. Done.

sara: after scale, queue_depth dropped to ~20 within 90s, throttle_events fell to single digits, tokens/sec normalized to ~28k. Latency improved.

liam: note: autoscaler logs show frequent small surges last week around 03:xx UTC from scheduled retrain job; could have primed caches.

anna: suggestion for post-incident work (ics):
- reduce noise: change autoscale alert from queue_depth > 100 to queue_depth > 90 with a 2m sustained window? Nah that's the opposite. We want fewer false positives -> increase threshold or require multiple signals.
- better: make alert composite: queue_depth > 100 AND tokens/s > 20k OR throttle_events > 5.
- add an annotation to the alert with suggested mitigations and playbook link.

sara: agree composite alert. Also add a cooldown for autoscaler so it can react quicker: lower the scale-up threshold to 90 OR increase scale step when tokens/sec rises > 30k. Current policy: step=+1 per 3m. Make step=+2 when tokens/sec spike detected.

liam: propose alert rule (PromQL):
```
ALERT AutoscaleQueueSaturation
  IF (
    max_over_time(queue_depth[2m]) > 100
    AND avg_over_time(rate(tokens_processed[1m])[2m]) > 20000
  ) OR increase(throttle_events[5m]) > 5
  FOR 2m
  LABELS {severity="page"}
  ANNOTATIONS {summary="Autoscaler likely undersized: queue_depth+tokens/sec or throttle spikes"}
```

anna: also add a non-paging slack alert for queue_depth spikes alone to eng-sre channel for visibility (no page unless composite triggers). Helps reduce noise.

sara: create a dashboard tile showing correlating axis: queue_depth, tokens/sec, throttle_events, scale_events, and pending_requests, with a linked timeseries for particular customer_id when throttles>0.

oliver: product asks that we tag scale_events and throttles with tenant_id if possible so we can show affected customers directly. Any privacy concerns?

liam: low-level logs already have tenant_id but we scrub for exported metrics. We can add a high cardinality label only for internal dashboards, not exported to public metrics. We'll annotate dashboards with tenant mapping, not in Prometheus label to avoid cardinality blowup.

sara: action items (immediate):
- liam: implement manual autoscaler step-change policy + lower scale-up latency (ETA today 18:00 UTC) [IN PROGRESS]
- anna: create composite paging alert + non-paging channel alert (ETA tomorrow) [TODO]
- sara: draft customer update & add to incident timeline (DONE)
- oliver: coordinate with support to close tickets once metrics stable (ONGOING)

liam: starting a short-lived feature flag to increase scale step for surge conditions. Will monitor.

incident-bot: PagerDuty: escalation created for this incident. Incident ID: INC-20240506-77. Assigned to oncall: sara.

sara: on-call handoff note: I'll be primary for next 2 hours, then handoff to liam for overnight. Leaving running watch in #eng-sre. If composite alert re-triggers, escalate to incident commander.

oliver: thanks team. For postmortem, please include timeline, metrics, alert tuning rationale, and cost impact of changing autoscaler params. Also add runbook update for model-burst patterns.

anna: logging a follow-up ticket: INFRA-678: Update autoscale alerts and dashboards; include sample queries and playbook references. Linked to incident INC-20240506-77.

sara: closing note: incident mitigated at 16:14 UTC, manual scale + fallback worked. We'll keep watch until 17:00 UTC and then file full postmortem.

liam: ack. Monitoring will stay on. Will post update when feature flag rollout completes.

sara: handing off at 17:00 UTC to liam. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

pagerduty: RESOLVED: INC-20240506-77 resolved by sara at 2024-05-06T17:12:34Z.
